A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Context Tuning work. All 22 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison across the changed formatting and numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracies, training times, ablations, Fisher-information estimates, and qualitative experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, robustness experiments, larger-model evaluations, and memory measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same CT-Prompt and CT-KV objectives, initialization, leave-one-out masking, token dropout, and TTT combination. Appendix D's CT-V and CT-Prefix variants also retain their procedures.

E1.justification: NLP-LR, MMLU, BBH, and ARC coverage is retained. Section 5.5 adds corrupted-demonstration-label scenarios on NLP-LR and MMLU, extending the input conditions evaluated without introducing new datasets or task domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds LoRA, Rank-Stabilized LoRA, and DoRA across all four benchmarks, substantially broadening the directly evaluated adaptation baselines. The existing prompt/prefix baselines and LoRA-based TTT comparator remain.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce demonstration-count sweeps, 0–100% label corruption, five 12B–32B backbones on BBH, and peak-memory profiling with batch size 1 for one epoch without accumulation or checkpointing. Original Table 1 settings remain unchanged. The new NLP-LR count setting is internally inconsistent: Section 5.5 specifies 4/8/12/16, while Figure 4(a) plots 8/16/24/32.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 and Figure 4 add substantive sensitivity tests concerning demonstration quantity and incorrect labels. Appendix F adds controlled memory-efficiency analysis. Existing component ablations, initialization studies, parameter-efficient variants, and qualitative case studies are preserved.

E5.justification: Matched results retain five-seed means and standard deviations, the ARC exception, and the existing mean-only appendix summaries. No new run-count or statistical estimation procedure is documented; Figure 4 and the larger-model Table 2 provide point estimates without specified uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 scores and matched appendix results are unchanged, but v2 adds baseline scores, robustness curves, larger-model accuracies, and memory measurements. For example, Table 2 reports Qwen32B scores of 69.1 for CT-KV, 63.1 for ICL, and 56.4 for Prefix Tuning. Table 12 reports BBH peak memory of 33,292 MB for CT-KV versus 54,752 MB for TTT under the new profiling protocol.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, Appendix A attention-complexity derivation, and Appendix D Fisher-information reasoning and prefix construction are retained. Added equation numbering and changes between inline and displayed mathematics do not change the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and central Context Tuning/ICO contributions remain stable. The conclusion adds explicit claims of superiority to LoRA variants, robustness to demonstration count and quality, and effectiveness with larger pretrained models.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new robustness and larger-model tests as evidence of broader applicability and adds an accuracy-versus-memory discussion in Appendix F. The cache-encoding explanation, ARC masking qualification, and overfitting limitation are retained.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the memory-profiling procedure and additional model checkpoints, and clarifies that the MetaICL comparison controls training and evaluation samples. Existing hardware, optimizer, learning-rate, iteration, and project-access information remains essentially unchanged; separate hyperparameters for the newly added LoRA variants are not supplied.

R1.justification: Five references are added for rank-stabilized LoRA, DoRA, Mistral NeMo, DeepSeek-R1, and Qwen3, supporting the expanded comparisons. The Related Work section and broader positioning of ICO remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. v2 inserts Sections 5.5–5.6 and Appendix F, condenses the conclusion, updates cross-references and affiliation text, and corrects the parameter-count row label from 'Context Tuning' to 'CT-V'. The overall narrative order remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redesigns the document template with a left-aligned title, shaded abstract, blue accents, running headers, and revised table styling and caption placement. It expands Table 1 and adds Figure 4 and Tables 2 and 12. Earlier figures and tables are retained with renumbering and reflow.

improvement.justification: The additional LoRA-family comparisons, larger-model evaluations, and controlled memory profiling strengthen evidence for the unchanged method's applicability and efficiency. This is a limited net improvement: the new demonstration-count study contains an unresolved Section 5.5/Figure 4(a) mismatch, and the larger-model results lack stated run counts or uncertainty, restricting confidence in parts of the expanded evaluation.
